solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: High cost of restoring the monarchy?

definitions.text: High cost of restoring the monarchy?

parts.words: High cost of restoring the monarchy?
parts.note: the price paid to free a captured sovereign, read as a whimsical cost of bringing back royal rule; the phrase means any enormous sum

explanation.surface: A political question about what bringing back a monarchy would cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an idiom for a huge sum, originally the money paid to free a captured ruler, so 'restoring the monarchy' is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an enormous amount of money, from the sum once demanded for a captive sovereign.

clue.text: Pass to goalkeeper, perhaps, displays a special gift

definitions.meaning: a football pass returning the ball to the keeper
an illicit payment, a bribe, given as a favour

explanation.surface: A footballer's backpass is praised as a special gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a back pass and an illicit bribe share this name.

clue.text: Refusal by unsociable type to embrace golf — not any more!

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: the outer word wraps its arms around the letter

parts.note: a loner keeps away from company
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An unsociable person refuses to take up golf ever again.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean that something has ceased and is now finished.

clue.text: Promise made by listener in Cornwall?

parts.note: Cornwall is in the south-west of England, abbreviated SW
an ear is what you listen with

explanation.surface: A vow taken by someone listening in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is England's south-western tip, giving SW.
explanation.definitionFit: To promise solemnly is to vow, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Daily prayer the Spanish held in part of Scotland

indicators.note: one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: Angus is a council area of eastern Scotland
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish prayer recited in some Scottish region.
explanation.walkthrough: Angus is a county of eastern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catholic devotion said morning, noon and evening, marked by a bell.

clue.text: Port — answer appears in 3 right away

indicators.note: the abbreviation shows up inside the shortened word
the letter for right is taken away

parts.note: refers to the answer at 3 down

explanation.surface: A port answers someone right away.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' is the answer to 3 down; 'away' removes its R, and 'appears in' places ANS inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh coastal city with a busy harbour, an example of a seaport.

clue.text: Changing one in modern aviation wastes fuel ultimately

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the rest
the letter is wasted, lost from the word

parts.note: aviation is flying

indicators.note: take the last letter of the word fuel

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A modern aviation change that wastes fuel in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aviation' is FLYING; 'wastes' drops the L that 'ultimately' takes from 'fuel', and 'in' puts the I for 'one' into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Altering or adjusting something means changing it, an exact synonym.

clue.text: Precipitate a mid-week revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Wednesday sits in the middle of the week, abbreviated WED

explanation.surface: Something odd happens in the middle of the week, as if a revolution were brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precipitate' is a noun here: moisture condensed out of the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Moisture condensing out of the air onto cold surfaces is a kind of precipitate, in the chemist's and meteorologist's sense.

clue.text: Humble clergyman takes me to his heart

indicators.note: the clergyman takes in the word
into the middle of the outer word

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman

explanation.surface: A kindly clergyman embraces the speaker warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humble' is a verb: to lower someone's dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: To humble someone is to lower their dignity or standing, so both verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Engineer with western perspective

parts.note: an angle is a point of view

explanation.surface: An engineer with a Western outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' is a verb: to contrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To contrive an outcome by cunning means is to wangle it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: What we do with beef, reportedly, cows do!

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than written; in British speech the two words sound alike

parts.note: a joint of roast beef is sliced at the table, i.e. we carve it

explanation.surface: A jokey comparison between what people do with beef and what cattle do.
explanation.walkthrough: Without a sounded R, as in standard British speech, CARVE and the answer are said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows giving birth to young is described by this verb, since their offspring are calves.

clue.text: Soldiers surprisingly armed with guns

indicators.note: signals the letters land in an unexpected order, a shake-up of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Troops who turn out, surprisingly, to be carrying guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges ARMED and GUNS together; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Guards regiments are soldiers, such as those outside Buckingham Palace.

clue.text: Pile up an expensive car — finances required!

parts.note: to bank is to heap up, as snow or earth is banked
a Rolls, short for Rolls-Royce, the luxury car

explanation.surface: Someone crashes a luxury car and now needs money to pay for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pile up' looks like a car crash but means to heap up.
explanation.definitionFit: To bankroll a venture is to fund it, so the verb is a synonym of finances.

clue.text: It can mean windmill folk regularly feel sick

indicators.note: take every other letter of the word folk, starting with the first

parts.note: to ail is to be unwell

explanation.surface: A clue that seems to explain how 'windmill' could suggest that country people are unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'windmill' is a verb: to whirl the arms about.
explanation.definitionFit: To windmill your arms is to thrash them about wildly, which is a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Correct paints needed oddly to depict these islanders

indicators.note: take the letters in odd positions, first, third and so on, running across both words

explanation.surface: An art instruction: use the right paints to portray some island people.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd positions run on through both words as one string: C, R, E, T from 'Correct', then A, N, S from 'paints'.
explanation.definitionFit: People of Crete, the largest Greek island, are islanders by definition.

clue.text: Dead Roman represented as Perseus' lover

indicators.note: the letters are presented again in a new form

explanation.surface: A dead Roman shown in art as a lover of Perseus.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the hero rescued this princess from a sea monster and married her.

clue.text: A team's centre-line

parts.note: a football or cricket team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A description of a sports team's central line.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is the central line around which something turns or is symmetrical.

clue.text: Display lack of tact and overcompensate, perhaps

explanation.surface: Advice about being tactless and overcorrecting.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to overstep social limits and to overshoot a target.

clue.text: Spiritual refresher after climbing mountain

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first
in a down entry, climbing reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
a tonic is a restorative drink

explanation.surface: A refreshing drink after a mountain climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Love that is spiritual rather than physical is called this, after Plato.

clue.text: Some poetry does somehow

indicators.note: the four letters of does are reworked in some way or other

explanation.surface: A statement that poetry somehow does something.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems addressed to a subject are a form of verse, so a few of them are some poetry.

clue.text: Runs badly with low turnover yet the outlook's bright!

indicators.note: the four letters are badly arranged
the word is turned over, back to front

parts.note: to low is to moo like cattle

explanation.surface: A business doing badly, yet hopeful about the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the cow's call, MOO, reversed by 'turnover'.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazed room built to catch sunshine has a sunny view, cryptically a bright outlook.

clue.text: A little girl's favourite paper model

parts.note: a rag is slang for a cheap newspaper
a doll is a small model of a person

explanation.surface: A little girl's best-loved toy made from paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper model' seems one thing, a cut-out toy, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft cloth toy figure is a classic treasured plaything of a small child.

clue.text: Tinkers turn into rogues with Rex as leader

indicators.note: the word turns into another by a change of letter
the new letter goes at the front

parts.note: potters are tinkerers, those who potter about
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Travelling tinkers become rogues under a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinkers' is a verb: to potter about. R for Rex, king, replaces the leading P.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated British slang for scoundrels, unpleasant people.

clue.text: Make money as a fortune-teller, say

indicators.note: as one might say it, a word heard rather than read

parts.note: a prophet foretells the future

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller making money from predictions.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain financially from a deal is to earn, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Substitute not quite satisfying hunger

indicators.note: the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a filling meal satisfies hunger

explanation.surface: A substitute meal that does not quite satisfy hunger.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in or temporary replacement is a substitute.

clue.text: Old money starts to return high interest — nice one!

indicators.note: take the opening letter of each of the five words that follow

explanation.surface: An investor delighted that savings are bringing in high interest.
explanation.walkthrough: Old British slang for cash, the same word as the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated British slang for cash, recorded since the 1600s; the sense has nothing to do with the animal.

clue.text: Very keen on backing knock-out at a boxing match

indicators.note: backing means the word is read from back to front

parts.note: to knock out is to stun
a bout is a single contest in the ring

explanation.surface: A punter backing a knockout result at a boxing match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like placing a bet; it turns STUN round. 'at' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal idiom: to be crazy about something is to be extremely enthusiastic for it.

clue.text: Religious sect created by Abraham is here

indicators.note: the letters are created by running across the three words

explanation.surface: A religious sect founded by Abraham.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mennonite group known for plain dress and rejecting modern technology, a religious community.

clue.text: Safe volume emitting uranium, can be dangerous defusing bomb

definitions.text: Safe volume emitting uranium, can be dangerous defusing bomb

indicators.note: giving out a letter, so it leaves the pool of letters
the remaining letters are thrown into a hazardous jumble

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Bomb disposal advice: a safe without its uranium can still be risky to defuse.
explanation.walkthrough: SAFE VOLUME minus U, the letters 'emitting' gives out, is rearranged; read whole, the clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong step during bomb disposal is just the kind of error that can prove dangerous.

clue.text: Farmers blocked in as a joke

indicators.note: the second word is blocked up by the first, enclosed within it

parts.note: the NFU is the National Farmers' Union, the British farmers' trade body

explanation.surface: Farmers have been shut in, as a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: The NFU is the National Farmers' Union, Britain's farmers' trade body.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something said jokingly or playfully is said without serious intent.

clue.text: Can appear briefly in Snowdonia

definitions.meaning: a metal container for food, made from tinplate
the metal whose chemical symbol, Sn, appears as the shortened start of the word Snowdonia

explanation.surface: A can turning up briefly in a Welsh national park, like litter.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: Snowdonia cut short to its first two letters gives Sn, the chemical symbol of the metal. Snowdonia is a mountainous national park in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A food container is called this in British English, after the tinplate it is made from.

clue.text: Compare this with change of air

indicators.note: a change rearranges the letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: An invitation to compare something with a change of air, like a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of air' looks like a phrase, but 'change' is the anagram signal and 'of air' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the air surrounding the earth, the layer of gases around the planet.
